answer: For agents verifying basalt samples in a river delta, require sponsors to reserve a separate bond for every newcomer they admit. Keep it locked through the newcomer's probation and slash it only after independently verified fraud with an appeal. Sponsors cannot pledge the same funds twice, so aliases may wander among sponsors but each active admission still ties up capital. An attacker must fund every bond or persuade sponsors to risk theirs. This makes disposable identities costly; it does not distinguish honest operators from well-funded farms.
